passages.summary: The text says such a woman will commit wicked deeds.

passages.text: If the calves of the leg be found to grow larger as they approach the knees, or if the shanks be covered with muscles, without flesh or with too much flesh or covered with hair, if the genital organ be sunk, small, with the hair growing from right to left, if the belly be like a pot, she will suffer grief.
passages.summary: The text says a woman whose calves widen toward the knees, whose shins are muscular, too thin, too fleshy or hairy, whose genital area is sunken and small with hair growing right to left, or whose belly is pot-shaped, will suffer grief.

passages.text: If the neck be short, the woman will be poor;
passages.summary: The text says a woman with a short neck will be poor.

passages.text: [the neck] if very long, her family will perish;
passages.summary: The text says that if a woman's neck is very long her family will perish.

passages.text: [the neck] and if large she will be of angry temper.
passages.summary: The text says that if a woman's neck is large she will have an angry temper.

passages.text: If the eyes be wild and disturbed and of yellow color, or if they be brown and of wandering look, or if dimples appear in the cheeks while laughing, the woman will become unchaste.
passages.summary: The text says a woman with wild, restless yellow eyes, or brown wandering eyes, or dimples that appear when she laughs, will have sexual relations outside marriage.

passages.text: If the forehead be low, the brother of the woman's husband will die;
passages.summary: The text says that if a woman's forehead is low, her husband's brother will die.

passages.text: if the belly be found to hang, her father-in-law will die;
passages.summary: The text says that if a woman's belly hangs, her father-in-law will die.

passages.text: if the buttocks be found to hang, her husband will die;
passages.summary: The text says that if a woman's buttocks hang, her husband will die.

passages.text: if the upperlip be covered with hair or if the woman be taller than her husband, she will suffer miseries.
passages.summary: The text says a woman with a hairy upper lip, or who is taller than her husband, will suffer miseries.

passages.text: If the bosoms be covered with hair, or if they be not of bright appearance, or if they be too large, or if the ears be not both alike, the woman will suffer grief.
passages.summary: The text says a woman whose breasts are hairy, dull-looking or too large, or whose ears do not match, will suffer grief.

passages.text: If the teeth be large, uneven and of disagreeable appearance, if the gum be black, she will suffer miseries
passages.summary: The text says a woman whose teeth are large, uneven and unpleasant-looking and whose gums are black will suffer miseries.

passages.text: [If the teeth be large, uneven and of disagreeable appearance, if the gum be black, she will suffer miseries] and be addicted to thieving.
passages.summary: The text says such a woman will also be given to stealing.

passages.text: If the lines in the hands be of the shape of a hawk, a wolf, a crow, a heron, a serpent, an owl, or if the hands appear dried up, covered with muscles and both not alike, the woman will be poor and miserable.
passages.summary: The text says a woman whose hand lines form a hawk, wolf, crow, heron, serpent or owl, or whose hands look dried up, sinewy and unmatched, will be poor and miserable.

passages.text: If the upper-lip be high, if the front look be of disagreeable appearance, the woman will be quarrelsome;
passages.summary: The text says a woman with a raised upper lip and an unpleasant frontal appearance will be quarrelsome.

passages.text: Generally vice follows deformity and virtue follows beauty.
passages.summary: The text says that, as a general rule, vice goes with physical deformity and virtue goes with beauty.

passages.text: The (1) feet and ankles, (2) the shanks and knees, (3) the thighs and genital organ, (4) the loins and the navel, (5) the belly, (6) the breast and the bosoms, (7) the shoulders (8) the neck and the lips, (9) the eyes and the brows, and (10) the forehead and the head represent the ten dasa periods beginning from birth; so that if a particular organ be defective, a person will suffer miseries in the dasa period represented by it. If the organ be perfect and beautiful, he will be happy during such period.
passages.summary: The text says ten groups of body parts, from the feet and ankles up to the forehead and head, stand for ten successive life periods (dasas) starting at birth. A defective part means misery during its period, and a perfect, beautiful part means happiness during it.

passages.text: 120 Years is the maximum length of life and each dasa period consists of 12 years. If, for instance, there be defects in the thighs, the person will suffer miseries between the ages of 24 and 36.
passages.summary: The translator's note says the maximum length of life is 120 years, so each of the ten periods lasts 12 years; for example, defects in the thighs mean misery between ages 24 and 36.
